_note: The PDB is demonstrated through its own STATUS, not by evicting a Pod: the Educates session role grants poddisruptionbudgets but not pods/eviction, and a node drain is the platform's action, not a tenant's. disruptionsAllowed 1 → 0 → 1 as the replica count crosses the floor is the observable, tenant-scoped proof. The timed deletion writes its measured seconds to /tmp/shutdown-seconds.txt for the check to read. verify-all-replicas-scheduled tolerates a single-node cluster on purpose — whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway is exactly what makes that case still work, and the check says which case it saw.

steps.run: envsubst < deployment.yaml | oc apply -f - && oc rollout status deploy/hello-dcs --timeout=240s
oc scale deploy/hello-dcs --replicas=2 && oc rollout status deploy/hello-dcs --timeout=180s
oc scale deploy/hello-dcs --replicas=3 && oc rollout status deploy/hello-dcs --timeout=180s

pod=$(oc get pods -l app=hello-dcs -o name | head -1); start=$(date +%s); oc delete "$pod"; end=$(date +%s); echo $(( end - start )) > /tmp/shutdown-seconds.txt; echo "deleting $pod took $(cat /tmp/shutdown-seconds.txt) seconds"
envsubst < deployment-spread.yaml | oc apply -f - && oc rollout status deploy/hello-dcs --timeout=240s
